finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST parameter 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents(), which accepts URLs (http, https, ftp, php://, file://, etc.). An attacker can make the server fetch internal hosts such as cloud metadata at 169.254.169.254 or localhost services. Local files can also be read via file://. The response body is not echoed, but its length is returned, which gives a blind oracle for probing internal ports and hosts and for timing and size side channels.

trace.note: Only checks that the request is POST and that 'feed' is set. No authentication.
$_POST['feed'] passed unvalidated to file_get_contents(), which performs the outbound request.
strlen($xml) is echoed back to the attacker, giving a response-size oracle.

finding.guards_checked: No require_admin() call on this path; it is defined at lines 4-9 but only used for set_webhook. No scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP or metadata-address blocking, no DNS-resolution check, and no redirect restrictions. None of these exist.

verdict.reason: import.php:12 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() with only an isset/POST check at line 11 (no require_admin, which is only used at line 18), and import.php:13 echoes strlen($xml), so the unauthenticated SSRF with a size oracle holds.

finding.claim: SSRF for admin sessions: the POST parameter 'set_webhook' is passed directly to curl_init() and executed with curl_exec(), with no scheme or host validation. An admin, or anyone who gets an admin session via XSS, CSRF or session compromise, can make the server request arbitrary internal URLs, including cloud metadata. curl also supports gopher://, file://, dict:// and similar. The response is not returned, so this is blind. Severity is lower because it requires admin privileges, and there is no CSRF token on the endpoint.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (HTTP POST body parameter, requires an admin session)

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is present.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin() session check only (line 18). No URL scheme restriction (CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS is not set), no host or IP allowlist, no private-range blocking, and CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION is not enabled but redirects are not the concern. No CSRF token.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session check only (import.php:18); no URL scheme or host validation.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate, but the sink at import.php:20-22 is reachable only after require_admin() (import.php:4-9, 18) confirms $_SESSION['is_admin'], so an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker cannot control $_POST['set_webhook'].
